chapter: Cavalcade, Wynonie Harris and the 1953 show
title: Chris Roustion the bass player as Harris's bouncer
summary: Bassist Chris Roustion was paid extra to rouse Harris out of hotel rooms and throw him in the car.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, he had a lot on the ball. And I had a bass player in the band named Chris Roustion, he was a big West Indian athlete, and was a bouncer. So (inaudible) get out of line, he was supposed to whip him. He was afraid of him. And he'd go (inaudible) go make a date drunk, he'd go there and break the door open, (inaudible). First he packed all his clothes, run all the women out of the room. He was scared of Chris. (Inaudible), you see. And that was his job, they were paying him extra to go roust him out.

And he'd go get the car and take him out, throw him across his shoulder and throw him in the car. And he finally got so he liked it. Let me get my clothes before this big sucker comes in here, this is my bodyguard. Get going, women. And he'd take and throw him in the car and drive him on off.

And a lot of times I'd stay with him and get him to another town. He was always getting arrested, always got arrested for bad language. So I don't know why he got into that, like that. That's what happened to him.
